name: Utopian Socialism
summary: Utopian socialism is the earliest current of modern socialism, associated with Saint-Simon, Fourier, Owen and Cabet. It condemns competitive, profit-driven industrial society and proposes cooperative, rationally planned communities in which labour and wealth are shared. Its adherents hope to win all classes by persuasion and the example of model communities, rejecting class struggle and political revolution.
scope: The early nineteenth-century school of Saint-Simon, Charles Fourier and Robert Owen (with Cabet's Icaria and the later colonies they inspired), as characterised by Engels and the Communist Manifesto and in Owen's own writings. It excludes Marxism, later Bellamy-style utopian fiction and anarchist or religious communitarian strands except where they overlap; the three founders differ (Saint-Simon technocratic, Fourier on passions and gender, Owen on education and circumstances), so answers follow their common core.

keyFigures.name: Robert Owen
keyFigures.role: Mill owner and reformer who built New Lanark and promoted cooperative villages.

keyFigures.name: Charles Fourier
keyFigures.role: French thinker who designed the phalanstery and made women's emancipation the measure of progress.

keyFigures.name: Henri de Saint-Simon
keyFigures.role: French thinker who divided society into workers and idlers and urged rule by science and industry.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Owen's national system for forming character and public employment imply communal provision of welfare, but healthcare as such was not addressed.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Owen backed hour limits in factories, yet wage floors were not a utopian method; they sought to replace wage labour with cooperative communities.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The Manifesto's utopians call for abolishing privately run industry and the wage system, and Owen blamed competition for misery.

public-ownership.rationale: Owen wanted machine-made wealth worked for the common good, but through community ownership rather than state nationalisation.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Utopians aimed to make the rich and poor alike join voluntary communities, not to redistribute through taxation, so the issue is peripheral.

unions-good.rationale: Owen helped found a great national trade union and promoted cooperation, though later Owenites distanced themselves from political labour action.

property-fundamental.rationale: Engels records Owen naming private property as a main obstacle to reform, and the communal systems abolish privately run industry.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Owen did support factory legislation, but the programme sought to replace firms with cooperative communities rather than regulate them.

cut-welfare.rationale: Owen held that poverty and crime come from circumstances and ignorance, and proposed public employment in slumps rather than withdrawing aid.

worker-ownership.rationale: Cooperative production and communities owning their common stock fit Owenite cooperation, though the community and not each workplace was the unit.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Owen preferred prevention and education to coercion; surveillance was not discussed, so this is inferred from his anti-punitive stance.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed by the founding utopians; their focus on rational training gives no clear direction on drug laws.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed; adherents' faith in education and benevolence points both ways on legal speech limits.

strong-leader.rationale: They relied on persuasion and example rather than force, though founders like Owen and Cabet often led their colonies personally and hierarchically.

state-harmful.rationale: The utopians wanted the state reduced to managing production, not abolished as harmful; Saint-Simon expected the administration of things to replace rule over people.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed; adherents' pacifist and anti-violence outlook suggests sympathy but no documented position.

empower-police-military.rationale: Owen sought to prevent crime by changing circumstances and not to expand punishment, so more coercive power is inferred as unwelcome.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Fourier prized sexual liberty and Owen condemned conventional marriage, but prostitution as such was condemned by Fourier as a product of civilization.

decide-locally.rationale: Their model societies were small self-governing communities such as phalansteries and villages of cooperation, with little role for national government.

rehabilitation.rationale: Owen argued crime springs from circumstances and that punishing it is unjust; he advocated prevention and rational training.

traditional-family.rationale: The Manifesto lists abolition of the family among utopian proposals, and Engels says Owen counted existing marriage an obstacle.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not addressed by Owen; Fourier's passional liberty hints at sympathy, but adherents did not take a stand on marriage law.

abortion-legal.rationale: The founding utopians did not address abortion.

more-religion-public.rationale: Owen counted organised religion an obstacle and favoured non-sectarian equal treatment, though Saint-Simon proposed a new Christianity.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not addressed; their universalist reforms would not oppose it but gave no programme.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Owen taught that character is formed by circumstances rather than innate nature, which extends to gender roles by inference.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: They addressed humanity as a whole and a single global order, so national tradition was not a concern.

gradual-change.rationale: They sought peaceful reform by example, yet aimed at complete transformation of institutions and opposed deference to existing ones.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Fourier foresaw universal unity and Owen universal benevolence, so restriction conflicts with their cosmopolitanism; not directly addressed.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Fourier envisioned a worldwide harmonious order but not through international organisations as such.

free-trade.rationale: Owen attacked competition and commerce for profit; free trade is inferred as at odds with cooperation.

nation-first.rationale: Their vision of universal harmony cuts against national selfishness, though never expressed in these terms.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Committed to peace and avoiding bloodshed, they would reject war for intervention; inferred.

open-borders.rationale: Universal unity is their ideal, but communities were small and voluntary and borders were not discussed.

limit-growth.rationale: Not addressed; Owen and Saint-Simon welcomed industrial productivity.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Owen saw machine-made wealth as able to serve everyone once worked for the common good, and Saint-Simon championed science and industry.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Anachronistic; the founders celebrated industrial progress but had no view on nuclear energy.

revolution-justified.rationale: The Manifesto says the utopians reject political and revolutionary action and seek change by peaceful means and example.

experts-over-public.rationale: Saint-Simon wanted politics as the science of production led by industrial and scientific leaders, and Fourier and Owen claimed a social science.

central-planning.rationale: Saint-Simon's directed production and Owen's planned communities suggest planning, but at the community level rather than a national command economy.

socialized-markets.rationale: Owen's labour-exchange bazaars used markets between cooperative bodies, but later utopians wanted their abolition; the question was not framed this way.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Saint-Simon wanted to end inherited privilege, but the group did not focus on taxation.

basic-income.rationale: Not proposed; they favoured guaranteed useful employment and communal provision over cash grants.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Saint-Simon had bankers direct production through credit, but Owen and Fourier relied on voluntary community investment.

widespread-small-property.rationale: They sought common property and association, not a society of small owners.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The Manifesto lists abolition of the wage system among their proposals, and Owen tried labour-note exchange as a step away from money.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Saint-Simon wanted bankers to regulate credit for production; abolishing central banks to leave money to the market is alien to the programme.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Saint-Simon's industrial hierarchy has corporatist echoes, but wages and prices set through state-recognised bodies is not their documented plan.

one-party-rule.rationale: They disclaimed political action and party struggle, relying on example and persuasion.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Saint-Simon courted rulers of any form to adopt reform, but the programmes were not monarchist and Owen distrusted hereditary privilege.

democracy-best.rationale: They addressed all classes and avoided political action; Saint-Simon's technocracy and Owen's paternalism make democracy a lukewarm commitment.

direct-votes.rationale: Not addressed; self-governing communities suggest some participation but no documented position.

workers-councils.rationale: They rejected political action by workers and so no soviet-style power basis; inferred.

right-to-secede.rationale: Communities were voluntary and seceding from them was possible, but state secession was not discussed.

natural-rulers.rationale: Saint-Simon wanted rule by industrial and scientific leaders and Fourier kept hierarchy and inequality in Harmony, whereas Owen stressed shaped character, so adherents split.

political-violence-never.rationale: Owen sought change without revolution, war or bloodshed, though absolute pacifism was not formulated.

war-builds-character.rationale: Fourier promised perpetual peace and Owen sought rational benevolence, so glorifying war is alien.

separate-church-state.rationale: Owen urged equal, non-sectarian treatment of religions in his community, implying no established sect.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Owen and Fourier built on reason and science, not scripture, though Saint-Simon's new Christianity and Christian utopians like Cabet differ.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Owen's preventive, communal approach to crime and faith in common provision contradict private security markets.

military-superiority.rationale: Universal unity and perpetual peace were central hopes.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Universal harmony and the equal formation of character sit against ethnic exclusivity; not directly addressed.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The Manifesto notes the utopians saw themselves above class antagonism and appealed to society as a whole.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Fourier said even in Harmony equality will not exist, while Owen sought common sharing, so the movement is split.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: The founding utopians never discussed indigenous land claims; neutral by silence.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Colonial reparations were never raised in the 1810s-40s utopian literature; neutral by silence.

civilizational-union.rationale: Universal association is their aim rather than regional civilization blocs.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Owen's principle was that each should contribute all in their power to the happiness of others, and Fourier condemned civilization's selfish competition.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Community and mutual duty are central, but the question of rights versus duties was not framed.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Fourier's cosmology gave nature a harmonic order, but adherents lacked an explicit intrinsic-value doctrine.

limit-population.rationale: Owen took a mildly Malthus-aware line in some writing, but the movement was split and he held poverty was social in origin.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Utopians criticised capitalist civilisation but sought to reorganise industry for common benefit, not abandon it.

accelerate-technology.rationale: They welcomed productive machinery but sought to restructure institutions, not disrupt them for its own sake.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Saint-Simon's science of production and administration of things is a distant analogue, but AI is anachronistic.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Anachronistic technology that the founders could not have addressed; neutral.

restore-past-order.rationale: They looked to a future social order built on science and association, not a return to the past.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Owen and others treated their plans as experiments proved by results in model communities, yet they held firmly to ideals.

direct-action.rationale: They disclaimed politics and used community-building and example, which resembles prefiguration but not protest or strikes.

means-match-ends.rationale: Their method was to build small model communities embodying the future society and persuade by example.

return-to-foraging.rationale: They counted on industry and science to produce abundance. The sources do not discuss primitivism directly.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Fourier's system rotated work among attractive tasks, which resembles it, whereas Saint-Simon retained specialised roles.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Fourier guaranteed a social minimum and Owen's communities held goods in common, but distributions often also rewarded labour, capital and talent.

production-for-use.rationale: Owen wanted productive forces worked for the common good, and utopians condemned production driven by profit and competition.

profit-exploitation.rationale: They condemned the profit system and idleness of non-producers, but Marx's exploitation analysis came later and Fourier even paid capital a share.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: They rejected political action and revolutionary class power, appealing to all classes.

collective-farming.rationale: Phalansteries and Owen's villages of cooperation combined agriculture in communal estates.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Owen blamed competition for conflict and Fourier foresaw peace under Harmony, but no theory of imperialism existed.

taxation-theft.rationale: Owen's communal goals and public employment schemes contradict an anti-tax stance.

harm-principle.rationale: Not addressed; adherents emphasised communal norms and shaped character.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Their stress on communal association and circumstances over individual desert makes this a poor fit.

conscription.rationale: Peace-oriented adherents would disfavour it, though not directly discussed.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Voluntary communities mean exit is available, but they relied on persuasion and community self-rule, not exit as the chief check.

state-as-business.rationale: Reducing the state to production management conflicts with treating citizens as customers of a competitive state.

positive-liberty.rationale: Owen held that circumstances shape people and that freedom to flourish requires education and employment, in line with material means.

media-academia-power.rationale: Not addressed; they prized education and the press as vehicles of reform.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Owen's central doctrine was that character is made by circumstances, which denies innate group differences.

organic-representation.rationale: Saint-Simon's industrial classes and Fourier's groups have some functional-representation flavour, but this was not a stated position.

total-state.rationale: They wanted small voluntary communities, not an all-directing state.

national-rebirth.rationale: They sought a new social order for all humanity rather than national renewal.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Their rational, scientific plans for society leave no place for rule by personal oaths. The sources do not discuss it directly.

bound-labor.rationale: They condemned exploitation and sought to emancipate labour, which excludes serfdom. The sources do not discuss bound labour directly.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: They believed in science and that rational training yields truth, though Owen held that knowledge shapes circumstances.

universal-morality.rationale: Owen thought rational principles of benevolence and truth could be taught to all, and Fourier claimed universal laws of social attraction.

single-common-good.rationale: They addressed society as a whole assuming their plan benefits everyone and stood above class conflict.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Not addressed by the founding utopians, though later cooperative settlements influenced kibbutz thinking.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Diaspora return rights were not part of the utopian programme; neutral by silence.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival was not a utopian concern; their aims were universal.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Cooperative production and communities governing their own industry imply a democratic say, though Saint-Simon preferred managerial direction.

school-vouchers.rationale: Owen called for a national, unexclusive system of education rather than parents choosing among private schools.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Not addressed; Owen proposed public employment in slumps, but fiscal doctrine was not theirs.

economic-freedom.rationale: They demanded abolition of privately run industry and wage labour, so economic freedom in the market sense is rejected.

rule-by-example.rationale: The Manifesto stresses their reliance on the force of example through model communities, and Owen emphasised moral training.

national-self-determination.rationale: Not a utopian theme; they envisioned universal harmony.

force-without-un.rationale: They sought to avoid war and bloodshed.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Owen and Fourier claimed a rational social science and criticised religion, though Saint-Simon and Cabet adopted a new Christianity.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Owen's universal benevolence suggests inclusion of all, though not directly addressed.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Saint-Simon held that all men ought to work and condemned idlers, and Owen stressed useful employment, though in cooperative form.

class-collaboration.rationale: The Manifesto says they appealed to the ruling class and all society and rejected class struggle.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Owen valued education and culture; this is a futurist position they did not hold.

dominated-front.rationale: Anti-Western fronts are a twentieth-century theme the utopians never addressed.

workers-nation.rationale: They were cosmopolitan, aimed at a universal order.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Fourier made women's emancipation the measure of general emancipation, and Owen attacked existing marriage.

ban-interest.rationale: Owen's labour-notes and Saint-Simon's credit system were not about banning interest.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Contradicts Owen's belief in environmental formation of character and universalism.

state-class-instrument.rationale: They did not hold a class theory of the state, standing above class conflict.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Anachronistic energy-policy question; the founders left no position.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Assimilation policy was not addressed in the founders texts; neutral by silence.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy theory with no basis in their outlook of benevolence.

proportional-representation.rationale: Not addressed; they were largely indifferent to electoral systems.

national-mission.rationale: They sought universal adoption through example, but some like Cabet and Owen hoped for model-to-world diffusion; not a national mission.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Fourier held that civilization's treatment of women is the measure of its progress, and Owen opposed marriage as then constituted.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: They avoided politics, addressing rulers as potential patrons.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Owen's doctrine that character is formed by circumstances rejects eugenic policy.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Transitional-justice questions were not addressed by the utopians; neutral.

night-watchman-state.rationale: They rejected laissez-faire and sought production organised for the common good.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Contradicts universal unity and Owen's environmentalism.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Owen's view that all character is made by circumstances and that all should be happy supports equal worth, though Fourier and Saint-Simon allowed hierarchy.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Their model communities were meant to spread by example without revolution; the statement is a Marxist-Leninist debate they did not join.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Not addressed; utopian colonies in America were themselves settlements.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Civil-law uniformity across religions was not a utopian issue; neutral by silence.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Owen advocated equal toleration of all religious groups.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A religious-cultural dietary law never raised by the utopian founders; neutral.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Owen wanted unexclusive, non-sectarian education, but did not take a clear stand on religious instruction.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist question they did not address; they expected the state to be reduced.

consent-of-governed.rationale: They relied on voluntary adoption by persuasion and example, which implies consent.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist trade balance goals were not addressed by the utopians; neutral by silence.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: They avoided force in changing society, but did not endorse an absolute non-aggression principle and Owen accepted hours legislation.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Owen and Fourier blamed competition for misery and set cooperation and association at the centre.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Not addressed; their toleration of dissent makes bans unlikely.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Not addressed in these terms, though their critique of dependence on employers has overlap.

separated-powers.rationale: Not addressed; constitutional design was not their concern.

vanguard-party.rationale: They saw the proletariat as undeveloped and relied on persuasion, not a revolutionary party; Marx's contrast makes this explicit.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Saint-Simon aimed at the most numerous and poorest class, and Owen's schemes began with relieving the poor.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Individual home ownership cuts against communal living in phalansteries and villages.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Owenites opposed Chartist political action but this was not legal doctrine.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Owen traced poverty to ignorance and lack of employment rather than population.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: His belief that proper training can give any community any character contradicts it.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Selection of officials by lottery was not a utopian proposal; neutral by silence.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Not addressed, though communal equality of status suggests sympathy.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Owen opposed coercive measures in favour of preventing causes of disorder; inferred.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Not addressed; labour exchange fixed prices by labour time but not for scarcity.

party-controls-media.rationale: They avoided party politics and favoured open education; inferred.

party-commands-army.rationale: They disclaimed party politics and war; inferred.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalisation rules were not addressed in the utopian programme; neutral.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: They did not organise political parties and rejected political action.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Universal association is their hope, though not through a particular union.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from peaceful and egalitarian views.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Owen opposed sectarian preference and Saint-Simon's new Christianity was hierarchic but not episcopal.

clerical-rule.rationale: Owen and Fourier relied on reason and science rather than clerics.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Not addressed; they were peace advocates but not revolutionary defeatists.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Owen shaped character through education rather than censorship.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Term limits for presidents were beyond the utopians concerns with political action.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall mechanisms were not discussed, since they avoided parliamentary politics.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Not addressed, though peace orientation is compatible.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Communal housing in phalansteries or villages is not individual family ownership.

people-in-arms.rationale: Citizen militias were not part of the programme of peaceful model communities; neutral.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: They proposed abolishing the divide between town and country and placed model communities on agricultural estates.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: National reunification was not a utopian issue; their aims were universal.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: They celebrated education as the main instrument of reform.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Fourier ranked societies in stages from savagery to Harmony, so they were not cultural relativists.

death-penalty.rationale: Owen argued that punishment is unjust because circumstances create crime, and favoured prevention. A New View of Society does not discuss capital punishment as such.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Owen's early education and Fourier's sexual openness point to sympathy, though not documented.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Owen's rational training and Fourier's science-based claims oppose it.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Not addressed; Fourier was sexually permissive but not on pornography.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Not addressed; Owen's toleration is compatible.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Fourier celebrated varied passions, but Owen emphasised shaped, harmonised character.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: International debt relief was not discussed in the founding utopian texts; neutral.

minority-language-support.rationale: Minority language policy was not addressed by the founders; neutral by silence.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Peaceful persuasion implies no coercion; inferred.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Universal benevolence supports it but it was not addressed directly.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Method of choosing a head of state was not addressed by utopians who shunned political action.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Not addressed, though Saint-Simon wanted bankers directing credit to production.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Peace was prized over territory; inferred.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Owen saw private property as an obstacle and wanted resources worked for the common good of all.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A later Marxist debate they did not address.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Anachronistic environmental doctrine the founders never addressed; neutral.

collective-defense.rationale: Military alliances were not addressed by peace-oriented utopians; neutral by silence.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Annexation law was not addressed in the founding utopian texts; neutral.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Owen opposed religious obstacles but did not propose state curbs on churches.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The role of a ceremonial head of state was not a utopian question; neutral.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Opposition to force suggests no; inferred.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Not addressed, though experimental autonomy is compatible.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Tax-rate structure was not a utopian concern; they sought to change production, not tax schedules.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Universal unity and shaped rather than inherited character sit against descent-based membership; not directly addressed.

character-from-environment.rationale: Owen's central doctrine in A New View of Society is that any character can be given to a community by proper means.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Utopian socialists sought rational, cooperative order by persuasion, not rule by a sovereign above law; inferred.

space-expansion.rationale: The utopians predate spaceflight and focused on earthly communities, so this is inferred as no position.

mixed-constitution.rationale: They proposed cooperative communities and rational administration, not a blend of few and many; inferred as split.

leader-cult.rationale: Their communities were meant to rest on reason and example, not on glorifying a leader, though followers revered founders; inferred.

equal-parenting.rationale: Fourier made women's emancipation the measure of progress, which suggests equal parental roles; custody was not addressed, so inferred.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: They rejected class struggle and held that all classes could be won over by persuasion, so a continuing struggle under socialism is foreign to them.

land-redistribution.rationale: Communities were to be founded by purchase and example, not by taking estates; inferred from their peaceful, non-expropriating method.

refugee-return.rationale: The founders did not address refugees; nothing in their principles points either way.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Fourier and Saint-Simon looked to universal unity and association, not national claims; inferred from that cosmopolitan outlook.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Owen held that belief is not a matter of will and that punishment should give way to rehabilitation, so punishing a change of belief contradicts his doctrine.

women-must-cover.rationale: Fourier demanded the liberty of women and measured progress by it; compulsory covering is inferred to be contrary to that.

common-currency.rationale: Not addressed; Saint-Simon wanted a European union of peoples, but Owen's labour money was local, so the school gives no common line.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Their unity was universal association of humanity rather than ethnic or linguistic union; inferred.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Not addressed; the model communities were self-governing, but national minorities were not their concern.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Not addressed; the colonies they inspired were founded abroad, yet no doctrine on persecuted minorities exists.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Engels and the Manifesto describe them as seeing history as the spread of reason and truth through example, not as the product of economic development.

ban-cartels.rationale: They condemned competition and the anarchy of production but not cartels as such, and looked to communities rather than state action; inferred.

no-bailouts.rationale: Not addressed; they hoped to replace competitive industry, not to rescue or refuse to rescue its failures.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The school stood aside from political action and constitutional questions, so there is no position to infer.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Fourier's liberty of women implies equal standing in public affairs, but quotas were not a method of the period; inferred.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Model communities aimed at being self-supporting, but a closed national bloc with colonies is not their proposal; inferred.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Owen campaigned for factory legislation limiting hours and child labour, so standards on labour are consistent with his reforms; trade agreements were not addressed.

moral-incentives.rationale: Owen and Fourier sought to make labour attractive and cooperative, replacing the profit motive, though Fourier kept rewards by capital, labour and talent.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The Manifesto says they rejected all revolutionary action and sought their ends by peaceful means and example.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Saint-Simon's industrial doctrine set the idle nobility against productive workers, and the school saw inherited privilege as an obstacle to rational organisation.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Owen wanted national education to form character, but it aimed at universal cooperation rather than national centrality; inferred as split.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Fourier and Owen held to universal unity and peaceful persuasion, which does not fit tutelage by rule; inferred.

patriotic-education.rationale: The founders aimed at universal harmony rather than national loyalty; inferred.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: The school never addressed it; its emphasis on circumstance and shared welfare does not settle the question.

public-money-creation.rationale: Owen and others proposed replacing money with labour notes in cooperative exchange, implying non-commercial control of money; inferred.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: They condemned competitive profit-driven society, though they hoped to replace it by example rather than by collapse; inferred.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Their ideal of universal unity cuts against national spheres of influence; inferred.

delink-world-market.rationale: Model communities were self-contained, but the founders took no position on world trade; inferred as split.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: They appealed to all classes and saw workers as sharing suffering under competition, not a divided class; inferred.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Their cooperative communities and belief that circumstances form character lean against free refusal to associate; inferred.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: They rejected political action and left constitutional design aside, so the question is peripheral.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Not addressed; the school focused on model communities, not boundaries.

elective-rulers.rationale: Saint-Simon favoured rule by industrial experts, while Owen and Fourier relied on persuasion and community self-governance; split.

minority-veto.rationale: Communities were to be run by agreement, but shared plans, not individual veto, govern; inferred.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The utopians rejected political revolution and appealed to rulers by persuasion, so resistance is not endorsed.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Owen sought reform through governments and Saint-Simon favoured technocracy; no stand on parliamentary supremacy.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Fourier and Owen stressed humane harmony with nature and compassion; inferred, not central.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Not addressed; inferred as split between harmonist concern for animals and acceptance of farming.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Owen and Saint-Simon appealed to the wealthy and powerful to improve the condition of the poor.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Utopians rejected political action and built separate model communities, which the Manifesto criticises.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Anachronistic; the school blamed circumstances and education for forming character, but not media.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: They believed all classes could be won by persuasion and example, not that rulers rule by cultural hegemony.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Anachronistic dependency thesis; the school criticised competition and commerce in general, not core-periphery transfers.

native-born-offices.rationale: Inferred from universalist, humanitarian outlook and invitation to all peoples to join communities.

party-own-road.rationale: Applies to later communist parties; the utopians offered no party doctrine.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Community self-sufficiency was central, but the utopians welcomed outside backing from wealthy patrons; split.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Inferred from their pacifism and universal fraternity, which oppose war over territory.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred from universalism and equality of persons and rejection of rank by birth.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Anachronistic; no basis in the school.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Anachronistic; no basis in the school.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Anachronistic historical dispute, though Owenite colonies in America were hostile to slavery; no strong inference.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred from their break with the old order and its symbols in favour of new rational institutions.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Fourier stressed women disadvantage; no stance on boys and men, so split.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Inferred from Fourier and Owen on equality of the sexes and rejection of cruelty, though women were the focus.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: They proposed one rational scheme of social organisation for all humanity.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Owen and Saint-Simon looked to industry and education, not armies, for order, and they were pacific.

paid-care-work.rationale: Fourier and Owen wanted domestic work socialised into communal arrangements, and Fourier made women free of household drudgery.

filial-duty.rationale: The Manifesto records the school's plans to abolish the family and Fourier's critique of the conventional family, so unconditional lifelong duty is inferred as disfavoured.

office-by-exam.rationale: Saint-Simon's technocratic strand put administration in the hands of those with scientific and industrial ability; the strand is not shared by all three founders, so inferred.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: The school's universal unity and cooperative harmony tell against national economic defence; inferred.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Fourier made the liberty of women and freedom of attachment a measure of social progress, so ending a marriage without proof of fault is inferred as agreed.

recallable-delegates.rationale: The school rejected political action and parties, so delegate mechanisms were not discussed; inferred as split.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Utopian socialists favour communal provision and cooperative security over private individual accounts; inferred.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The model communities hold land and capital in common and Owen's villages are communal property, as the Manifesto and Engels describe.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The school rejected political action and so did not address parliamentary control of budgets.

single-official-language.rationale: The school's national education plans imply a common medium, but its universal harmony does not address language rights; inferred as split.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Universal unity and peaceful fraternity tell against restricting land ownership by foreigners; inferred.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Owen held that character and outcomes are formed by circumstances rather than individual fault, so unequal outcomes would be read as a social defect; inferred.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Owen and Fourier condemn competitive, profit-driven society and favour simple shared living, so consumer excess is inferred as harmful.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Utopian socialists sought change by persuasion and example and rejected violent revolution, so arming rebels is inferred as opposed.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: The school relied on peaceful persuasion and universal fraternity and rejected force, so forcible intervention in allies is inferred as strongly opposed.

corporate-influence.rationale: Condemns competitive, profit-driven commerce as corrupting society; influence of business over government is inferred from that critique.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Foreign funding of NGOs was not an issue for the school; no position can be inferred from its principles.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Fourier and Owen planned communal child-rearing but did not discuss population policy or immigration; inferred as no stance.

residents-only-property.rationale: Model communities hold land in common and admit members by association, so limiting land to residents is inferred as consistent.

job-guarantee.rationale: Owen proposed employing the poor in cooperative villages and Fourier asserted a right to work; the state-as-employer framing is inferred.

democratic-peace.rationale: The school did not address regime types; Saint-Simon wanted a peaceful European union, but the democratic-peace claim itself is not theirs.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: They sought to win rulers and all classes by persuasion and rejected political revolution, so civil disobedience is not their method; inferred.

non-intervention.rationale: Saint-Simon proposed a European association of nations for peace, implying cooperative rather than strictly non-interfering relations; inferred.

industrial-unions.rationale: The school predates mass industrial unions and sought to replace wage labour with cooperative communities, so the craft versus industry question is not addressed.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: They appealed to all classes and rejected class struggle; Fourier voiced prejudices, but a secret minority plot is not part of the doctrine.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Owen condemned marriage founded on property and Fourier attacked monogamous marriage as an institution; inferred as favouring its removal from law.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Owen's plan relied on open education and publicity of the new system; inferred support for open access to information.

local-production.rationale: Phalansteries and Owenite villages were designed as largely self-sufficient communities producing mainly for their own members.

informal-organisation.rationale: They rejected parties and political struggle in favour of voluntary small communities of like-minded people; inferred.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Saint-Simon looked to European and industrial association above national governments; inferred, not stated on international law.

religious-nation.rationale: Owen rejected organised religion as a cause of social ills and the model communities were not defined by creed; inferred.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the movement's appeal to all of humanity by reason and example, with no place for tribute hierarchies among states.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from communities that pool labour and wealth for the common good rather than guard local revenue.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Inferred: the model communities hold land, tools and production in common while the Engels account gives no sign of abolishing personal belongings.

defeat-communism.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the creed's reliance on peaceful persuasion and example rather than force against rival systems.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Inferred: Owen's national schemes and communal institutions are run by the community itself, not by competing private providers.

religion-illusion.rationale: Adherents split: Owen attacked organised religion as an obstacle to reason, while Saint-Simon proposed a New Christianity.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: They condemned competitive industrial society but valued its productive power as the means to abundance; adherents are mixed.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Fourier made the position of women the measure of social progress and called for their liberty within a reorganised society.

socialized-care.rationale: Fourier's phalansteries and Owen's communities provide communal kitchens, nurseries and infant schools in place of private household work.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the universalist, cosmopolitan outlook of the founders.

treaties-binding.rationale: The early founders did not address treaties with internal nations; no answer follows from their principles.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Founding small self-governing communities with shared property is the movement's defining method.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred from voluntary, peaceful and universalist aims; no state steering of settlement.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Inferred: they condemned competitive capitalism and sought a new cooperative order, though communism as a rival system came later.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Utopian socialists were universalist and built communities open to all; claims of peoples to land by history are inferred to be alien to them.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Anachronistic and never addressed; inferred rejection from their humanitarian, rationalist universalism.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Fourier defended the free expression of varied passions and Owen held people not to blame for their character; inferred, not a stated policy.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The Manifesto says they rejected political and revolutionary action and relied on peaceful persuasion and example, so coercing opponents is foreign to the method.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Owen held that people are not responsible for their beliefs because circumstances form them, which makes punishing them irrational; inferred.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: They condemned exploitation of labour and sought cooperative equality; ruling overseas territories for one country's benefit is inferred as contrary to this.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: An Islamic religious duty outside the movement's horizon; no position inferred.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: They rejected violent political struggle of any kind and Owen was hostile to organised religion, so forcibly removing rulers over religious law is inferred as rejected.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Owen's villages and Fourier's phalanxes were self-governing cooperative communities, but Saint-Simon was technocratic, so adherents are not uniform; inferred.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Fourier made the liberation of women a measure of social progress and all tied oppression to social arrangements, but class, race and sex were not theorised together.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Anachronistic; Fourier's tolerance of diverse passions suggests sympathy but the question was never raised.

assisted-dying.rationale: Not addressed by the founders; no position can be inferred.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The Manifesto says they appealed to all of society without distinction of class and rejected class struggle, which fits combining the ideas of different camps; inferred.

alienated-labor.rationale: Fourier proposed making labour attractive because existing work is repugnant, and Owen condemned the factory system's effect on workers; the term alienation is later.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Their universal brotherhood and belief that character is shaped by circumstances would reject essentialist cultural incompatibility; inferred.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Owen was hostile to organised religion and Fourier rationalist; Saint-Simon's later New Christianity is an exception, so inferred at low confidence.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Not addressed; the movement's rationalism and tolerance point in different directions.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: A modern employment-law issue never raised by them; no position inferable.

social-market-economy.rationale: They condemned competitive profit-driven society and sought to replace it with cooperative communities, not to regulate it, though they worked in reform spirit.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: They sought universal peace and harmony and saw war as a product of competitive society; inferred sympathy, not a stated programme.

rich-first.rationale: They aimed to share wealth in cooperative communities and criticised inequality, though Saint-Simon rewarded by capacity.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Anachronistic; the movement had no view on great power blocs.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Inferred from rationally planned, cooperative communities and equal membership; the founders appealed to rulers but did not defend hereditary office.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Owen's labour exchanges and the cooperative communities replaced profit trading with exchange at cost, but a user-owned bank was not a stated plan.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the rejection of profit-driven commerce and finance in favour of cooperative organisation.

property-franchise.rationale: Inferred from the aim of winning all classes and sharing wealth in common; suffrage rules were not their focus.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Fourier championed women's emancipation, but he and Saint-Simon looked to mastering nature through industry, so the combined claim does not fit.

reification.rationale: Inferred from their condemnation of competitive society in which commerce rules human relations; the term is later Marxist.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Inferred from their critique of competitive society and the power of wealth; the press was not a theme.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: They aimed at administration and model communities by persuasion, with little interest in constitutional law, so the question is not addressed.

racial-franchise.rationale: Their appeal to all humanity and equal membership in communities makes ethnic exclusion foreign to the school; inferred.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic and not addressed by the early nineteenth-century founders.

open-government-data.rationale: Not addressed; the founders were technocratic or communal planners without a view on open records.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Inferred from Owen's hostility to religious divisions and his appeal to a common human character; not stated for marriage law.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Inferred from their universal fraternity and persuasion of all classes; targeting a minority is opposed to this.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Owen and Fourier ran model communities by collective deliberation among ordinary members, though Saint-Simon preferred expert rule; inferred from that common communal-participation core.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Saint-Simon recast Christianity as a New Christianity serving the poor, and the founders sought a rational, modernised moral religion; inferred, as Owen was hostile to religion generally.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Owen, Fourier and Saint-Simon condemned competitive industrial society's gulf between rich and poor and proposed shared property and labour.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Anachronistic; Fourier's rejection of sexual repression suggests tolerance, but military service was not addressed.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Utopians rely on persuasion and education rather than state coercion, and Saint-Simon and Cabet gave religion a place; inferred mild disagreement.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Utopians aimed to remove the causes of crime through education and environment, as Owen held, but did not call for abolishing police or prisons now; inferred.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Not addressed; the movement disliked political struggle and had no theory of constitutional power sharing.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Utopians proposed communal provision for the poor within cooperative communities and did not choose between charity and state aid in the modern sense.

term-limits.rationale: Not addressed; utopian socialists focused on model communities rather than electoral institutions.

vote-delegation.rationale: Anachronistic; utopian communities favoured direct cooperative decision-making but the idea is not in the sources.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Not addressed; the movement hoped for progress through rational reform but did not discuss extinction risk.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Fourier argued that the degree of women's emancipation measures social progress, and Owen's movement backed women's equality; religious office is an inference.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Fourier and the Owenites attacked the legal subjection of women in marriage and held that women's emancipation is the measure of social progress.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred from Fourier's ideal of universal unity and Owen's appeal to all classes and nations.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred: the school wanted cooperative provision and curbs on profit, so it would back limits on rents.

abolish-ip.rationale: Not addressed; the school proposed communal property in communities, so patents were not an issue.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred: Owen's education aims to form character by gentle example, not drill.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Inferred from Owen's peaceful reform and aversion to violence; nuclear arms are anachronistic.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred from the school's peaceful aims and rejection of political conflict.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Inferred from its humanitarian universalism; the school did not address recognition.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Engels reports Saint-Simon's contrast of workers with idlers who live on property income, and Owen's aim of common labour and wealth.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Owen sought rehabilitation over punishment and peace, but the school did not address self-defence; inferred as split.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Inferred: Fourier's universal unity treats nations as parts of one human harmony.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Inferred from Owen's view that circumstances form character and Fourier's critique of women's condition.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred: Fourier is a champion of women's liberty but the school did not address the category.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred: the school sought persuasion and peaceful reform and did not look to martyrdom.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Engels notes the school's rational, secular planning; politics is for them a matter of reason and example.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Not addressed by the school; inferred as split.

culture-before-state.rationale: Inferred from the school's belief in education and example before political action, as the Manifesto's account has it.

god-not-male.rationale: Not addressed; Saint-Simon turned to a New Christianity while Owen opposed religions; inferred as split.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Fourier measured progress by women's liberty, but the school did not judge scripture; inferred as split.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Owen's appeal to all classes and Fourier's universal unity exclude control of the economy by one national group.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Inferred: the school planned small communities and universal unity, not ethnic territorial units.

independent-unions.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the movement's reliance on voluntary association and persuasion rather than state direction.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The founders rejected class struggle and political action and hoped to win all classes by example, so they did not make workers' own political power the test of socialism.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Inferred from the communal provision of needs in the planned communities, which treat basic services as shared.

second-chamber.rationale: Inferred from the aim of replacing political government with rational administration of communities, which leaves little role for a second legislative chamber.

municipal-property.rationale: The model communities hold property and the means of labour in common among their members rather than privately or through a national state.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Inferred from the plans to link model communities in wider cooperative unions by example and consent; the sources do not detail this.

family-wage.rationale: Inferred from the principle that the community provides for the needs of all its members, not only for the work each performs.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Anachronistic; the founders' faith in science points one way and their caution about hasty change the other, so no stance can be inferred.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Inferred from the founders' faith in science and rational organisation to improve human life.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Anachronistic; nothing in the sources bears on private payments, and the communities' proposals on money do not settle it.

online-anonymity.rationale: Anachronistic; nothing in the sources bears on online identity, so there is no basis to lean either way.

person-over-state.rationale: Inferred from Owen's and Fourier's aim of making communities serve each member's happiness and passions, though Owen's view that circumstances form character also stresses the collective.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Fourier's passional attraction and Saint-Simon's New Christianity treat human nature as more than material, but Owen rejected religion, so adherents differ.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Anachronistic; the founders designed self-governing communities rather than regional devolution within a nation state.

gm-crops.rationale: Anachronistic; the sources give no basis for a stance on genetic engineering.

dense-cities.rationale: Inferred from the model communities being planned mixed agrarian and industrial settlements that aimed to abolish the opposition between town and country.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The movement rejected group conflict and appealed to all humanity; race as a basis for organising is not addressed.

racial-pride.rationale: Inferred from the universalist appeal to all classes and peoples; pride in race is not addressed.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Owen and the others sought change by peaceful persuasion and example, which implies force only for defence, though war policy is not discussed.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Inferred: the founders pursued universal harmony and cooperation across all classes and countries, not nationhood based on language.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred: they sought to unite everyone in shared communities, so separate religious electorates cut against the project.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Inferred: the founders appealed to all classes and nations by example and showed little interest in foreign plots.

free-public-college.rationale: Owen urged a national system of education for all, so free public higher education is an inference from that principle.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Anachronistic: the founders did not address pollution pricing, and their planned communities would have used design rather than taxes.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred from the aim of building lasting model communities and harmony for posterity; not discussed directly.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Fourier demanded women's liberty but as equality of rights, and the sources do not say women bring distinct values; adherents differ.

arms-reduction.rationale: Inferred from Owen's peaceful reform and the movement's rejection of conflict; arms limits are not discussed.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Inferred from the movement's reliance on open persuasion and example rather than political manoeuvre.

capital-controls.rationale: Inferred from planned, communal economies in which money and exchange are subordinated to the community.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: The school proposed peaceful cooperative communities and had no stated view on armed groups; inferred as split.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Owen and the school sought peaceful reform and treated war as a product of bad circumstances, so soldiers refusing state wars fits, but it is inferred.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Owen's cooperative ideal and the school's rejection of competition favour common rules among workers, though they put weight on cooperative communities rather than bargaining; inferred.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: The school wanted to replace the wage system with cooperative communities and never addressed tax top-ups; inferred as split.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Not addressed by the school, which concentrated on founding communities; inferred as split.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Fourier's universal unity and the school's appeal to all classes imply fairer terms between nations, but there is no programme on trade rules; inferred.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The Manifesto says utopian socialists rejected all political, and especially revolutionary, action and relied on example and persuasion. They hoped existing rulers and patrons would adopt their plans rather than smash the state, so the answer is inferred.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: The school promoted experimental communities, which suggests openness, but each founder wrote a detailed blueprint for the right system, so adherents are split.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Inferred: the school wanted rational, cooperative use of the earth, not pricing it, but it never discussed ecosystems as capital.

sacred-nation.rationale: Fourier's universal unity and the school's cosmopolitan appeal to humanity leave no place for a sacred nation; inferred.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Owen's national education plan implies public support for learning, so relieving student debt fits; inferred.

internal-colonialism.rationale: The school criticised inequality within industrial society but did not frame it in regional or colonial terms.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Owen's central claim is that character is formed by circumstances and can be remade by education and environment, though Fourier took the passions as fixed.

public-service-media.rationale: Owen's view of education and public enlightenment suggests support for publicly funded media; inferred.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Owen thought all religions rest on error, while Saint-Simon and Cabet stressed a new Christianity and Fourier a universal harmony; the founders differ, so this is split.

farm-price-support.rationale: Never addressed; communities were to be self-sufficient cooperative settlements rather than market participants, so state price guarantees are not a natural fit.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the school's hope of replacing competition and conflict with harmony and cooperation, which points to disarmament.

workers-own-party.rationale: Utopians distrusted class politics and appealed to all classes, including rulers, rather than building a workers' party; Engels and the Manifesto criticise exactly this.

ban-fgm.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Fourier's and Owen's concern for women's dignity and welfare and the rationalist rejection of harmful custom.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Fourier made the degree of women's emancipation the measure of social progress and advocated equal rights, though property was to be communal in most schemes.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Not addressed; a linguistic classification question with no bearing on the school.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Inferred: the school rejected competitive private-property society and planned cooperatively, so it would not rest harms on individual lawsuits against polluters.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred from the rationalist, planned reorganisation of society by experts and communities, which gives no role to inherited customary authority.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Not addressed in the founders; communities valued harmony with nature, but also stressed free development of individuals, so it is split.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Owen held that character is formed by circumstances, so punishment is irrational and crime is to be cured by education and environment, which opposes fixed punishments.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Not addressed; communities were open to voluntary members and the school was internationalist, so this is inferred as neutral.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Inferred from the founders' preference for cooperative, collectively organised labour; unions as such were not addressed in the founding texts.

voter-id.rationale: Electoral mechanics were not addressed; the school rejected political struggle in favour of persuasion and model communities, so it is indifferent.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred from Owen's rationalist, universalist case that all creeds and classes can be won over; the school did not legislate on religious law.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Inferred: the school put social organisation and example above political forms, so electoral procedure alone would not make a government legitimate.

premarital-sex.rationale: Fourier built his system on liberating the passions, including a freer amorous life for women, and attacked conventional marriage morality.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the school's reliance on persuasion and benevolent reform rather than coercion.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the preference for communal provision and organised employment over individual cash transfers.

women-suffrage.rationale: Fourier held that the liberation of women is the measure of social progress; equal political rights were not spelled out, so the answer is moderate.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Fourier and Owen criticised conventional morality and marriage, but Saint-Simon and Cabet were religious, so adherents are split.

race-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from Owen's doctrine that character is formed by circumstances and upbringing, which undercuts innate group differences.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred from the school's concern with women's emancipation and planned social institutions; dedicated agencies were not discussed.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the movement's rejection of private property and competition in favour of shared land and wealth in communities.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Anachronistic: the founders favoured peace and persuasion but never discussed international courts, so this is inferred as neutral.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Owen attacked organised religion and Saint-Simon and Fourier built rationalist systems, though Cabet and some followers were Christian, so this is inferred.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Fourier held that the status of women measures social progress and Owen's communities gave women a role; Indigenous self-government itself is anachronistic.

defend-planned-state.rationale: The founders favoured planned cooperative communities but rejected political revolution and never faced a bureaucratic state, so this is inferred as split.

indirect-election.rationale: Owen's plans for federated communities hint at delegated bodies but the founders gave no settled view and Saint-Simon preferred expert rule, so this is split.

national-church-status.rationale: Inferred from Owen's hostility to established religion and the movement's rationalist, universalist outlook.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: The movement never addressed ethnic autonomy; its model communities were voluntary and not based on ethnicity, so this is inferred as neutral.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Not addressed by the founders, so this is inferred as neutral.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Not addressed by the founders, so this is inferred as neutral.

simple-living.rationale: Owen, Fourier and Cabet's communities stressed modest, shared living, but Fourier promised abundant pleasure, so the inference is mild.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Anachronistic: the founders planned colonies, some in America, but never addressed Indigenous settlement restrictions, so this is split.

equal-conscription.rationale: The founders were pacifist-leaning and never discussed conscription for women, so this is inferred as neutral.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Inferred from the founders' universal aims, such as Fourier's universal unity, which put humanity above national attachment.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Owen argued that circumstances form character and urged rehabilitation over punishment, which excludes killing people without trial.

close-ties-china.rationale: Anachronistic; the school did not discuss foreign alignments.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Inferred from Fourier's universal harmony and the school's appeal to all humanity, not to a nation.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the shared property and common labour of the proposed communities; compensation to others is not discussed.

self-ownership.rationale: Owen holds that circumstances shape character, while Fourier stresses liberty of passions; inferred and split among the three founders.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Anachronistic; the school proposed communities, not tax policy.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Inferred: Owen proposed national education and the communities share provision among all members, not only the poorest.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Inferred: the school rejected political action and class struggle and relied on persuasion and example, so the question mostly does not arise.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Inferred from their condemnation of competitive, profit-driven society.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Saint-Simon proposed a new religion and Owen opposed existing churches; the school never addressed denominational politics.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Inferred: Saint-Simon and others looked forward to rationally planned industrial society, not a return to ancestral values.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Fourier championed the liberty of women, and Engels credits the school with attacking women's subjection in marriage.

national-resource-control.rationale: Anachronistic; the school aimed at self-governing communities rather than national resource policy.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Utopian socialists proposed shared wealth and equal provision to remedy the injustice of competitive society, which cuts against judging by process alone; inferred.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Anachronistic; the school condemned speculation and commerce but never proposed such a tax, so this is inferred as neutral.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Owen held that character is formed by circumstances and that educational reform can remove social evils, and they opposed oppression; inferred from that.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Utopian socialists sought change by persuasion and example rather than by legal theory; no common view on law's authority, so this is inferred as split.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Fourier and Saint-Simon looked to industry and science to give abundance and shorten toil, and Owen praised machinery; inferred from their optimism about production.

multipolar-world.rationale: The school founded model communities and gave little attention to the balance of states; Saint-Simon wanted European union, so this is inferred as split.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Owen argued that labour is the source of wealth and proposed labour notes, though Fourier rewarded capital and talent as well; adherents lean agree.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: The school addressed all humanity and all classes rather than nations, so patriotism is not part of it; inferred as neutral.

material-over-identity.rationale: Anachronistic; the school stressed both material welfare and the remaking of character, family and sexual relations (Fourier), so this is inferred as split.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Utopian socialists rejected both competitive markets and political party struggle in favour of cooperative communities; inferred.

missingStatements.text: Social change should be pursued by founding small model communities that show a better way of life, rather than by political struggle.
missingStatements.rationale: The Manifesto and Wikipedia describe reliance on the force of example through experimental communities such as New Lanark, phalansteries and Icaria as the movement's defining method.

missingStatements.text: A person's character is formed mainly by their circumstances and upbringing, so society can be reshaped by changing education and environment.
missingStatements.rationale: Owen's central doctrine in A New View of Society is that any character can be given to a community by proper means.

missingStatements.text: Work should be organised so that it is attractive, and society should rotate people among tasks according to their passions.
missingStatements.rationale: Fourier's system of passional attraction is built on making labour agreeable, a defining feature of the phalanstery.
missingStatements.declined: Fourier-specific design of labour; abolish-division-of-labor does not capture it and it is too niche to ask of every ideology.

notes: Saint-Simon's hierarchical technocracy, Fourier's retention of unequal shares and Owen's egalitarian communism differ; answers on equality, expertise and religion therefore partly split. Marx and Engels judged the school utopian because it appealed to all classes and rejected political action.
